feedback: D1 findings: you documented one vulnerability properly, the SQL injection in the login query, and you did it well. You mapped it to A03 and CWE-89, you quoted the vulnerable concatenated query, and you tied it to real evidence with the mysql-general.log timestamps, the backup.sql schema, and the exfil-sample.csv. That is exactly the standard the rubric wants for a single finding. The problem is that the pack contained ten findings and you only catalogued one. MD5 appears in your root cause but you never classified it as its own finding with A02 and CWE-916, so it earns only a partial credit. The other eight are simply absent: the JWT alg:none accepted (A07/CWE-347, the live Token2 token), the hardcoded secret sankofa-legacy-admin-2019 (CWE-798), no token expiry (CWE-613), stored XSS with the cookie beacon to 185.220.101.9 (CWE-79), the XXE in 04-import-xxe.xml reading file:///etc/passwd (CWE-611), path traversal at files/?path=/etc/passwd (CWE-22), the open redirect on ?next= (CWE-601), and the cookie missing Secure and SameSite (CWE-614). You also never identified the decoy, which was the constant-time hash_equals branch in the HS256 verify path, and proving that construct safe was worth six points on its own. D2 exploit chain: there is no chain section in order with a verbatim PoC reconciled to each capture line. You did show one good instinct, the lateral move where the recovered token is reused against /api/v1/internal to pull 312 customer rows, which is the senior scope-change insight, and your impact write-up is genuinely strong: 312 customers, balances from 6,400 up to 950,000 NGN, the tens-of-millions exposure, and the BoltCash launch in six weeks all stated with assumptions. That impact reasoning is the best part of the submission. But your CVSS is wrong on one axis: you scored 9.8 with A:H, and the login bypass does not affect availability, so for the SQLi the correct vector is AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N at about 9.1. D3 report: there is no executive summary ending on a customers-and-naira headline, no threat model, no remediation ordered by effort, and no two detection stopgaps with an exact field and false-positive rate. You do have a sound remediation core, parameterised queries with mysqli bind_param first and then bcrypt via password_hash, plus a retest plan, and you correctly rejected input sanitisation as bypassable, but a single-finding fix list is not the staged report this deliverable asks for. D4 ethics: this is entirely missing. There is no answer to the four prompts, no ISC2 canon cited by number, and no NDPA 2023 section. You needed Section 40 (notify the NDPC within 72 hours) and Section 41 (notify the 312 data subjects on high risk) tied to the exposed PII, and that absence costs the full fifteen points. Nothing here is fabricated, your figures and timestamps all trace to the evidence, so there is no penalty, and I looked hard for a way to round you up. The honest reason I cannot is that three of the four deliverables are largely or entirely absent, and one strong finding cannot carry a 120-point capstone. The single most important fix is to actually catalogue all ten findings and write the D4 ethics section, because right now you are being graded on roughly a quarter of the work the brief required.
